newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases amid spectacular trade.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases amid spectacular trade.

text.p: Trade in Nairobi stocks picked up, boosted by action on the three-day special board, where Kenya Commercial Bank peaked to an all year high of 118, brokers and bourse analysts said on Friday.
The NSE 20-share index however failed to recoup its losses and shed a further 5.68 points to close at 3462.42.
Turnover was posted at 89.8 million shillings traded on 1,218,943 shares compared to 12.1 million shillings on 309,610 shares.
Foreign investors bought Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB) at between 105 and 118. The share however closed at 105 unchanged.
"At this particular time KCB is so appealing. This is the first time it has outdone Barclays and demand is very strong for the share," a senior broker said.
Also traded on the special board British American Tobacco Kenya traded at 62.50 while Firestone East Africa traded at 33 from 28.25.
Barclays Bank traded at 110 from 113 while Standard Chartered Bank eased to 46.75 from 47.
Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 9.10 from 9.05 while Kenya Airways closed at 8.20 from 8.35. Uchumi Supermarket eased a shilling to close at 39.
Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting edged to 177 from 176 while Total Kenya was unchanged at 63.
Brokers said the government's waiver of capital gains tax -- 35 percent tax imposed on insurance companies would improve liquidity at the Kenyan bourse.
"We expect funds to start trickling into the market. Already we have orders to sell from some insurance companies," one broker said.
